System avoided costs System avoided costs are modeled using the Avoided Cost Calculator (ACC). The ACC determines the economic benefits of DERs including energy efficiency and demand response. The model quantifies the benefits in terms of avoided generation capacity, energy, ancillary services, GHG emissions, and transmission and distribution capacity for each climate zone and utility. We take 2019 and 2030 total marginal costs from the ACC and, for 2030, conduct a “day- matching” exercise such that the times of high marginal costs align with times of high system net load in our load forecast model. This involves first determining cost weights for each hour- month combination and then reallocating these costs across days based on the corresponding load levels. Figure 6 shows the average daily shape of the avoided costs compared to an illustrative set of price profiles. In general, hourly marginal avoided costs are much lower than our hourly dynamic prices, as prices represent the full cost of providing electricity to customers, inclusive of non- marginal costs. The avoided cost stream is also much more concentrated in peak summer evening hours, further illustrated in Figure 7, whereas dynamic prices are fluctuating across the entire year. Particularly in 2019, avoided costs are extremely concentrated in a small portion of 20 hours, primarily in September. The top 31 hours are all in September from 6pm-11pm; these hours are all around $1000/MWh or above (with the peak reaching $6880/MWh), while the 32nd highest hour is $613/MWh. Therefore, avoided cost results are expected to be higher for cooling loads that are more coincident with the high-cost hours, and generally lower than customer bill savings across the board.
